pipeline.attack_summary: The Slingshot APT uses a complex attack platform involving Mikrotik router compromise via Winbox Loader to download malicious DLLs like ipv4.dll, which acts as a downloader for other components. It employs kernel-mode modules such as Cahnadr/NDriver and user-mode GollumApp for persistence, data exfiltration, and evasion. The malware uses vulnerable drivers to load into kernel mode and hides its encrypted file system from defragmentation.

indicators.context: The name appears unencrypted in some of the malicious samples – it is the name of one of the threat actor’s components, so we decided to extend it to the APT as a whole.
The initial loader replaces the victim's legitimate Windows library 'scesrv.dll' with a malicious one of exactly the same size.
One of them – ipv4.dll – has been placed by the APT with what is, in fact, a downloader for other malicious components.

When the target user runs Winbox Loader software (a utility used for Mikrotik router configuration), this connects to the router and downloads some DLLs (dynamic link libraries) from the router’s file system.
Following infection, Slingshot would load a number of modules onto the victim device, including two huge and powerful ones: Cahnadr, the kernel mode module, and GollumApp, a user mode module.
Canhadr, also known as NDriver, contains low-level routines for network, IO operations and so on.

The most sophisticated module is GollumApp. This contains nearly 1,500 user-code functions and provides most of the above described routines for persistence, file system control and C&C communications.
During our research we also found a component called KPWS that turned out to be another downloader for Slingshot components.
These vulnerabilities include CVE-2007-5633; CVE-2010-1592, CVE-2009-0824.

attack_vector.reasoning: The text clearly describes a phishing email with a hyperlink leading to the malware download, which is the initial access vector. The subsequent behavior of the malware is well-documented including execution, persistence, and C2 communication.

pipeline.attack_summary: The attack begins with phishing emails containing hyperlinks that lead to downloads of NetWire RAT malware. The initial payload is often disguised as a PDF or document, and once executed, the malware uses anti-analysis techniques like dynamic code extraction and anti-sandboxing to avoid detection. It then establishes persistence via registry keys, collects system information, and communicates with a C2 server using DNS resolution for IP address discovery. The malware supports over 80 commands including credential theft, file operations, keylogging, and process control.

title: Initial Access via CVE-2023-22518 Confluence Auth Bypass
id: 7a9e4f1c-1b6d-4c3a-9e2f-3a1b5d8e2f7a
status: experimental
description: Detects exploitation of CVE-2023-22518 by observing unauthenticated POST requests to Confluence setup-restore endpoints with X-Atlassian-Token header set to 'no-check', indicating an attempt to bypass authentication and reset the system.
references:
    - https://confluence.atlassian.com/security/cve-2023-22518-improper-authorization-vulnerability-in-confluence-data-center-and-server-1311473907.html
    - https://www.huntress.com/blog/confluence-to-cerber-exploitation-of-cve-2023-22518-for-ransomware-deployment
    - https://github.com/ForceFledgling/CVE-2023-22518
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1548/002/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1078/004/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1566/001/
author: Sigma Assistant
date: 2026-10-16
tags:
    - attack.initial-access
    - attack.privilege-escalation
    - attack.t1078.004
    - attack.t1548.002
    - attack.t1566.001

    category: webserver
detection:
    selection1:
        cs-method: 'POST'
        cs-uri-stem|startswith: '/json/setup-restore'
    selection2:

falsepositives:

level: high

    - attack.t1548.002

pipeline.attack_summary: The Lazarus group conducted two separate attacks targeting a government health ministry and a pharmaceutical company. The first attack used wAgent malware, deployed via command-line execution with rundll32.exe, which fetched additional payloads from C2 servers and established persistence using AppCert DLLs. The second attack used Bookcode malware in a supply chain attack against the pharmaceutical company, leveraging compromised web servers for C2 communication and performing post-exploitation activities including credential dumping and lateral movement.

Analysis and Report by Fabian Marquardt (@marqufabi) - Recently, Telekom Security CTI was made aware via trust groups in which we are engaged about a new malware campaign that is distributed via phishing emails. The malspam campaign used stolen email threads to lure victim users into clicking the contained hyperlink, which downloaded the malware. Attention to this malware campaign was also fueled by a false attribution of one of the malware samples to Emotet. Even though this attribution later turned out as a false positive match of an automated detection rule, it caused the security research community to focus on this new campaign. Initial analysis quickly revealed significant similarity to the DarkGate malware, based on the use of a similar initial infection routine (AutoIt scripts) and the observed C2 communication protocol, which matched past analyses of the same malware family.
The AutoIt script is bundled with the.au3file extension which is usually used for plain-text scripts. Instead it contains a pre-compiled script, which would typically use the.a3xextension.

For this infection chain, the initial payload is self-contained, meaning that all further payloads are embedded into the file and that no further payloads need to be pulled from external sources to complete the DarkGate infection. Specifically, the file contains an AutoIt executable and a corresponding script which is executed by the installer. Application Verifier x64 External Package - UNREGISTERED - Wrapped using MSI Wrapper from www.exemsi.com

The script will spawn acmd.exeshell usingShellExecuteand use thecurlbinary that is shipped by default in current Windows installations to download an AutoIt executable and a corresponding AutoIt script.

DllCall("user32.dll", "lresult", "C"&chr(97)&"llWindowProc", "ptr", DllStructGetPtr($MFCKuCoyGW), "hwnd", 0, "uint", 0, "wparam", 0, "lparam", 0)

The script can be decompiled usingmyAut2Exe(a pre-compiled binary can be foundhere) after renaming the file from.au3to.a3x. Analysis of the decompiled script shows that the sole purpose of the script is to execute a shellcode that is contained as a hex-encoded string: The screenshot above only shows an excerpt of the complete sequence to create the shellcode string. This string is then decoded to binary data and written to a newly allocated memory area using theBinaryToStringandDllStructCreatefunction calls. Finally, two commands are executed. These commands are obfuscated as hex-encoded strings. Decoding these strings reveals their purpose, which is to make the newly allocated memory area executable withVirtualProtectand call the shellcode usingCallWindowProc:

rules_yaml:
title: VMware vCenter Server Analytics Service File Upload Attempt
id: 7b6e4a9d-3f8c-4b2a-a0d1-7e5c9a8f1b2d
status: experimental
description: |
    This rule detects unauthenticated file upload attempts to the vCenter Server analytics service endpoint (/analytics/service) via HTTPS. 
    The attack leverages CVE-2021-22005, a file upload vulnerability in VMware vCenter Server that allows remote code execution.
    The rule targets the HTTP POST request with multipart/form-data content type to the specific analytics endpoint.
references:
    - https://www.tenable.com/blog/cve-2021-22005-critical-file-upload-vulnerability-in-vmware-vcenter-server
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1190/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1210/
author: Sigma Assistant
date: 2026-10-16
tags:
    - attack.initial-access
    - attack.t1190
    - attack.execution
    - attack.t1210
logsource:
    category: webserver
detection:
    selection_method:
        cs-method: POST
    selection_uri:
        cs-uri-stem: /analytics/service
    selection_header:
        cs-header|contains: multipart/form-data
    condition: all of selection_ *
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate administrative uploads to the analytics service (if any)
level: high

pipeline.attack_summary: SOURGUM (Candiru) is a private-sector offensive actor using 0-day Windows exploits (CVE-2021-31979 and CVE-2021-33771) to deliver DevilsTongue malware via single-use URLs sent through messaging apps like WhatsApp. The malware achieves persistence via COM hijacking, drops encrypted configuration files in system directories, and uses a legitimate signed driver (physmem.sys) for kernel-level operations. It steals credentials from browsers and Signal, and can send messages as the victim.

pipeline.attack_summary: Stealth Falcon uses a zero-day vulnerability (CVE-2025-33053) in .url files to execute malware from an attacker-controlled WebDAV server. The attack chain involves initial access via spear-phishing emails containing malicious .url attachments, which exploit path traversal to run iediagcmd.exe and route.exe from the WebDAV server. The route.exe loader uses code virtualization, memory manipulation techniques (WriteProcessMemory, SetThreadContext), and IPfuscation to inject shellcode into Edge browser processes. It also deploys custom implants based on Mythic C2 framework including the Horus Agent, which supports commands like survey, shinjectchunked, and upload.

title: Initial Access via Malicious SESSID Cookie in GlobalProtect
id: 5a8c7b4d-9f2e-4a3c-b8d0-1e9a6f7b8c9d
status: experimental
description: Detects an unauthenticated attacker sending a crafted HTTP request with a malicious SESSID cookie value to the GlobalProtect login endpoint, which is the primary attack vector for CVE-2024-3400.
references:
    - https://security.paloaltonetworks.com/CVE-2024-3400
    - https://labs.watchtowr.com/palo-alto-putting-the-protecc-in-globalprotect-cve-2024-3400/
    - https://attackerkb.com/topics/SSTk336Tmf/cve-2024-3400/rapid7-analysis
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1190/
author: Sigma Assistant
date: 2026-10-16
tags:
    - attack.initial-access
    - attack.t1190
logsource:
    category: webserver
detection:
    selection:
        cs-uri-stem|startswith: /global-protect/
        cs-cookie|contains: SESSID=
        cs-cookie|re: SESSID=.*`.*?
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate administrative tools using crafted session cookies for testing
level: high

title: Command Injection via Device Telemetry in GlobalProtect Exploitation
id: 6b9d8c5e-0a1f-5b4d-c9e1-2f0b7c8d9e0f
status: experimental
description: Detects execution of curl command with IFS variable for space replacement in device telemetry, indicating successful exploitation and command injection via CVE-2024-3400.
references:
    - https://security.paloaltonetworks.com/CVE-2024-3400
    - https://labs.watchtowr.com/palo-alto-putting-the-protecc-in-globalprotect-cve-2024-3400/
    - https://attackerkb.com/topics/SSTk336Tmf/cve-2024-3400/rapid7-analysis
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1068/
author: Sigma Assistant
date: 2026-10-16
tags:
    - attack.execution
    - attack.t1068
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        CommandLine|re: curl.*\$\{IFS\}
        Image|endswith: \\curl.exe
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate administrative scripts using curl with IFS for command execution
level: high

id: 1a3e5f7c-9b4d-4a6e-8b2c-1d9e8f7a6b5c
status: experimental
description: |
    This rule detects the initial access phase of CVE-2020-0688 exploitation by identifying a crafted POST request to /owa/auth.owa with valid credentials, followed by a GET request to /ecp/default.aspx containing a malicious __VIEWSTATE parameter.
    The attack uses authenticated low privilege to exploit a deserialization vulnerability in Microsoft Exchange Server.
references:
    - https://www.trustedsec.com/blog/detecting-cve-20200688-remote-code-execution-vulnerability-on-microsoft-exchange-server/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1190/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1078/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1203/
author: Sigma Assistant
date: 2026-10-16
logsource:
    category: webserver
detection:
    selection1:
        cs-method: 'POST'
        cs-uri-stem: '/owa/auth.owa'
    selection2:
        cs-method: 'GET'
        cs-uri-stem: '/ecp/default.aspx'
        cs-uri-query|contains: '__VIEWSTATE='
    condition: selection1 and selection2
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate administrative scripts using valid credentials to access Exchange ECP
    - Automated monitoring tools accessing ECP endpoints with ViewState parameters
level: high

pipeline.attack_summary: Raspberry Robin is a worm that initially spread through infected USB drives containing LNK files disguised as folders. Upon insertion, it executes cmd.exe to launch msiexec.exe which installs malicious payloads from compromised QNAP NAS devices. It uses living-off-the-land binaries (LOLBins) like rundll32.exe and regsvr32.exe for execution and persistence, and injects into system processes. The malware also deploys other malware families such as FakeUpdates, IcedID, Bumblebee, and TrueBot, leading to follow-on hands-on-keyboard attacks and ransomware deployment.

title: Initial Access via Malicious SSH Certificate with ED448 Backdoor Payload
id: 5a7e6d9c-3f2b-4c1a-9d8e-0f1a2b3c4d5e
status: experimental
description: Detects the use of a malicious SSH certificate containing an attacker-controlled N value in the CA signing key, which triggers backdoor execution via ED448 signature validation. This rule targets the primary attack vector involving initial access through vulnerable OpenSSH server.
references:
    - https://github.com/amlweems/xzbot?tab=readme-ov-file
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1190/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/004/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1552/004/
author: Sigma Assistant
date: 2026-10-16
tags:
    - attack.initial-access
    - attack.t1190
    - attack.t1021.004
    - attack.t1552.004
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'xzbot'
            - 'ed448'
        ParentProcessName|endswith:
            - '\sshd.exe'
            - '\ssh.exe'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate use of xzbot for testing or debugging purposes
    - Authorized penetration testing involving SSH certificate manipulation
level: high

title: Execution of Backdoor Command via System Call After ED448 Signature Validation
id: 6b8f7e0d-4a3c-5b2d-0e9f-1a2b3c4d5e6f
status: experimental
description: Identifies execution of commands through the system() API call, which is used by the backdoor triggered during ED448 signature validation. This indicates that the malicious payload has been decrypted and executed on the target system.
references:
    - https://github.com/amlweems/xzbot?tab=readme-ov-file
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/004/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1203/
author: Sigma Assistant
date: 2026-10-16
tags:
    - attack.execution
    - attack.t1059.004
    - attack.t1203
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'system()'
            - 'id > /tmp/.xz'
        Image|endswith:
            - '\xzbot.exe'
            - '\sshd-xzbot.exe'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate scripts using system() for command execution
    - Authorized administrative tasks involving shell commands
level: high

title: Potential Atlassian Confluence CVE-2021-26084 Exploitation Attempt
rules_yaml:
title: Exploitation of CVE-2021-26084 Confluence OGNL Injection
id: 5a3b7c9d-e8f2-4a1b-9c4d-0e5f6a7b8c9d
status: stable
description: |
    This rule detects exploitation attempts of CVE-2021-26084, an OGNL injection vulnerability in Atlassian Confluence Server and Data Center.
    The attack targets the /pages/createpage-entervariables.action endpoint with a queryString parameter containing OGNL expressions,
    allowing unauthenticated remote code execution. Detection is based on web server logs capturing HTTP requests to this vulnerable path
    with attacker-controlled input patterns indicative of exploitation.
references:
    - https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2021-26084
    - https://confluence.atlassian.com/doc/confluence-security-advisory-2021-08-25-1077906215.html
    - https://github.com/h3v0x/CVE-2021-26084_Confluence
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1190/
author: Sigma Assistant
date: 2026-10-16
tags:
    - attack.initial-access
    - attack.t1190
logsource:
    category: webserver
detection:
    selection:
        cs-uri-stem: '/pages/createpage-entervariables.action'
        cs-uri-query|contains: 'queryString'
        cs-uri-query|contains: '${'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate administrative scripts using the same endpoint with valid parameters
level: high

title: Execution of CVE-2021-26084 Mitigation Scripts
id: 9f8e7d6c-5b4a-3c2b-1a0f-9e8d7c6b5a4f
status: stable
description: |
    This rule identifies execution of scripts used to mitigate CVE-2021-26084, a known OGNL injection vulnerability in Confluence Server.
    These scripts are typically executed post-compromise or during patching operations. The detection is based on process creation logs
    showing invocation of either cve-2021-26084-update.sh (Linux) or cve-2021-26084-update.ps1 (Windows).
references:
    - https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2021-26084
    - https://confluence.atlassian.com/doc/confluence-security-advisory-2021-08-25-1077906215.html
    - https://github.com/h3v0x/CVE-2021-26084_Confluence
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/007/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/003/
author: Sigma Assistant
date: 2026-10-16
tags:
    - attack.execution
    - attack.t1059.007
    - attack.t1059.003
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\cve-2021-26084-update.sh'
            - '\cve-2021-26084-update.ps1'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate patching or maintenance activities using these scripts
level: medium
